title: What the request-based Schedule II partial fill requires of each actor
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.13(a) the stock-shortage partial fill is permissible only if the pharmacist MAKES A NOTATION OF THE QUANTITY SUPPLIED on the face of the written prescription, in the written record of the emergency oral prescription, or in the electronic prescription record. The REQUEST-BASED pathway in 1306.13(b) allocates duties to both actors. Its general conditions in (b)(1) are conjunctive: the partial fill is not prohibited by State law; the prescription is written and filled in accordance with the Act, the chapter and State law; the partial fill is requested by the PATIENT, by one acting on the patient's behalf (a parent or legal guardian of a minor, or a caregiver of an adult patient named in a medical power of attorney), or by the PRACTITIONER who wrote the prescription; and THE TOTAL QUANTITY DISPENSED IN ALL PARTIAL FILLINGS DOES NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL QUANTITY PRESCRIBED. Under (b)(3), a practitioner who wants the prescription partially filled MUST SPECIFY THE QUANTITY TO BE DISPENSED IN EACH PARTIAL FILLING on the face of the written prescription, in the written record of the emergency oral prescription, or in the electronic record; after consultation with a pharmacist the practitioner may authorize a partial fill at a later date, but the prescription must still be filled not later than 30 days after it was written, or 72 hours for an emergency oral prescription. Under (b)(4) a request may be made in person, in writing if signed by the requester, or by telephone; and WHERE THE PRACTITIONER HAS ALREADY SPECIFIED QUANTITIES UNDER (b)(3), the patient, guardian or named caregiver MAY NOT REQUEST A PARTIAL FILLING GREATER THAN THE AMOUNT THE PRACTITIONER SPECIFIED. Under (b)(5) the pharmacist's notation differs by requester: a practitioner request made in consultation is noted as 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill' with the practitioner's name, the date and time of the discussion and the pharmacist's initials, while a patient, guardian or caregiver request is noted as that named person having requested the partial fill on a stated date, together with the quantity dispensed. Every request-based partial filling also generates a dispensing record carrying the date, the name or initials of the dispenser, and the other elements 21 CFR 1306.22(c) requires for Schedule III and IV refills; for electronic prescriptions that information must be LINKED to the electronic prescription record.
exam_relevance: Tests who may ask for a partial fill, what the practitioner must have specified in advance, the ceiling a patient request cannot exceed, and what the resulting record must contain in each pathway.

authority.name: Request-based partial filling, conditions and records

exceptions: The stock-shortage notation under 1306.13(a) is only the quantity supplied; the fuller request-based notations belong to 1306.13(b)(5).
A consultation-authorized partial fill adds the 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill' notation that a partial fill specified on the face of the prescription does not require.
Where the practitioner has specified per-fill quantities, a patient-side request cannot exceed them.
The remaining-portion period is 30 days from writing, except 72 hours where the prescription was an emergency oral one.
common_confusions: Treating partial-fill notation as a Massachusetts-only duty when federal law imposes its own notation in every pathway.
Recording only the quantity on a request-based partial fill and omitting the requester and the date of the request.
Overlooking that the total across all partial fillings may not exceed the total quantity prescribed.
Assuming a patient may request any quantity, when a practitioner's advance specification caps it.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.13(a) and (b)(1)-(b)(5) read verbatim in the current eCFR text on 2026-09-10. v2 adds the practitioner-side half of the request-based pathway -- the per-fill specification, the cap a patient request cannot exceed, and the total-quantity condition -- which the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V6A audit found absent from SG-CII-LIFECYCLE with no prescriber duty stated anywhere. The rule is cited only by that unpublished section and by no question, so the bump moves nothing. Independent audit still required.
